newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: New Congo free plane impounded for Kabila "insult".
newsitem.headline: New Congo free plane impounded for Kabila "insult".

text.p: Authorities in Kinshasa have released a plane impounded after South African pilots "insulted" then rebel leader Laurent Kabila, now president of Democratic Republic of the Congo, negotiators said on Thursday.

The South African owned Lear jet was rented at the time by U.S. mining company, American Mineral Fields, who offered its use in May to Kabila for a trip to South Africa from Lubumbashi, said the negotiators employed by LLoyds' underwriters.

"The plane took off just as Kabila arrived on the tarmac," said Christopher Newman of Defence and Management Associates, a London-based company specialising in recovering property lost in complicated circumstances.
"It was considered the pilots had insulted President Kabila and when the plane returned from a roundabout journey it was impounded," he said.

Newman said the South African owners of the plane had since proved unable to secure its release despite help from the South African foreign ministry. They had filed a claim of $800,000 to Lloyds', who sought help from Newman's firm.

"At first the authorities wanted the pilots to come back to apologise. But in the end they released the plane with no attachments. I think they felt that enough attention had been brought, with London, and South Africa involved," he said.
